correctness.rationale: After two moves, equality, adjacency and the set of third-point incidence patterns are the exact one-round invariant. At order at least seven a distinct vertex adjacent to neither named vertex always exists. For adjacent distinct vertices, the remaining neighbors coincide precisely on a triangle; for nonadjacent ones the common-neighbor counts 0, 1 and 2 have distinct pattern sets, with count 2 precisely at opposite vertices of a square. Hence the set of pair types extending a vertex identifies triangle, square or longer cycle; each admits a far partner by another component or by distance at least three. Taking sets once more gives exactly the three cycle-presence bits, with no counting of multiplicities. A dominating pair separates all five small cases from the large orders. Triangle existence, a nonadjacent pair, nonadjacent twins, and a nonadjacent pair with no common neighbor provide the stated small-case distinctions. The minimum orders for the seven large signatures are attained by cycle partitions as listed; the full signature costs at least 3+4+5 vertices and has only one partition at that minimum. The square witness uses a universal third quantifier, but is indeed rank three. A fresh exact recurrence on adjacency/equality patterns reproduced 12 fingerprints across 572 partitions through order 24.
residual_risks: Finite replay does not establish orders beyond 24; all orders are covered by the game recurrence argument. The empty graph and signatures with additional predicates are outside scope.
